question: Why does the review recommend dissolving the aluminium foil in an alkaline solution to separate the cathode materials?

runs.text: The review does not recommend this. It presents alkaline dissolution of aluminium foil as unsustainable. Its reasoning is that recovering the current collectors (Cu and Al) matters because copper smelting is a major source of SOx and other greenhouse gas emissions in the cradle-to-gate stages of the battery life cycle. The review states that
dissolving Al in an alkaline solution is not a sustainable separation method.

support.quote: in an alkaline solution is not a sustainable separation method

runs.text: The review instead points to non-alkaline options for detaching cathode coatings from Al foil, such as molten salt, deep eutectic solvents and ethylene glycol, while noting that the PVDF binder was not removed in those studies.

rendered: The review does not recommend this. It presents alkaline dissolution of aluminium foil as unsustainable. Its reasoning is that recovering the current collectors (Cu and Al) matters because copper smelting is a major source of SOx and other greenhouse gas emissions in the cradle-to-gate stages of the battery life cycle. The review states that dissolving Al in an alkaline solution is not a sustainable separation method.[1][2] The review instead points to non-alkaline options for detaching cathode coatings from Al foil, such as molten salt, deep eutectic solvents and ethylene glycol, while noting that the PVDF binder was not removed in those studies.
